Topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read

Target audience: University students with basic programming/math background

Section: section_1 — The Problem: Context Blindness

Lecture lines:
Context is hard for simple models to maintain.
'The bank' needs 'river' to be understood.
Old models forget context over long distances.

Planned animations:
Fade in text "Query", "Key", "Value" at top of screen with color #FFFFFF.
Display a central vector representation and animate Query approaching it with color #FF5733.
Animate Key vector aligning with Query, changing to color #33FF57.
Animate Value vector being weighted by the alignment score with color #3357FF.
Fade out all elements to transition to the final concept with color #888888.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)

Lecture lines:
We use a library catalog analogy for retrieval.
Query is what you want to find.
Key is the label on the shelf.
Value is the content inside the book.
QKV enables intelligent information lookup.

Planned animations:
Fade in Q, K, and V matrices with distinct colors #FF5733, #33FF57, and #3357FF.
Highlight Q and K matrices individually to emphasize their role with color #FFFF00.
Simulate the matrix multiplication Q*K^T with a bright flash effect in color #FFFFFF.

Section: section_3 — The Mechanism: Calculating Attention Scores

Lecture lines:
Dot product measures similarity between two vectors.
Query multiplied by Key gives raw attention scores.
High scores mean more focus on that word.
'It' pays attention to 'cat' over 'mat'.
This creates our attention heatmap.

Planned animations:
Display the attention score formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(dk))V with color #FFFFFF.
Flash the term QK^T / sqrt(dk) to emphasize scaling with color #FF5733.
Show the transformation process of scores into probabilities with color #33FF57.
Visually map the probabilities to weighted Values with color #3357FF.
Consolidate the entire process into a single block with color #CCCCCC.

Section: section_4 — Softmax and Weighting

Lecture lines:
Scores can be large and unmanageable.
Softmax maps scores to a zero-one range.
Attention becomes a probability distribution.
The spotlight highlights relevant words clearly.
Weights sum up to one perfectly.

Planned animations:
Fade in the score vector with values [2, 1, -1] in color #FFFFFF.
Apply Softmax to the vector, showing the values transition to probabilities with color #FF5733.
Visualize the final weights being applied to the Value matrix with color #33FF57.

Section: section_5 — Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture

Lecture lines:
One attention head is rarely enough.
Parallel heads capture different types of relationships.
One head tracks grammar, another tracks tone.
Combining heads provides a complete understanding.
Multi-head attention mimics human cognition.

Planned animations:
Split screen into four smaller regions for different heads with color #FFFFFF.
Animate each head performing its own attention calculation in colors #FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF, #FFFF33.
Show the results of each head being concatenated together with color #FFFFFF.
Project the concatenated output into the final representation vector with color #CCCCCC.
Final display highlighting the combined result across all heads with color #FFFFFF.

Flash central vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bank.svg] as Query approaches in #FF5733.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
